newsitem.title: USA: President Clinton leads Dole by 18 points - poll.
newsitem.headline: President Clinton leads Dole by 18 points - poll.

text.p: President Bill Clinton has a lead of 18 percentage points over Republican challenger Bob Dole in the 1996 presidential race, a New York Times/CBS News poll shows.
The poll, released late on Thursday, shows Clinton has strong approval among voters for his stewardship of the economy, a key electoral issue.

The survey indicates 54 percent of registered voters would vote for Clinton if November elections were held today. Thirty-six percent would vote for Dole and 8 percent support billionaire third-party candidate Ross Perot.
In the modern era of political polling no presidential candidate with a double-digit advantage around the Labour Day holiday at the start of September has lost the election.
Fifty-seven percent said they approved of Clinton's performance as president, against 31 percent who disapproved.
The survey indicates 55 percent of Americans back Clinton's handling of the economy, the highest rating he has received for this area of government.
Seventy-two percent of those polled said the U.S. economy was in good shape, against 27 percent who said it was in bad condition.
The poll was taken from Monday evening through Wednesday evening among 1,281 adults. It has a margin of error of plus or minus 3 percentage points.
A Reuters poll released Thursday showed Clinton had a 15 percentage point lead over Dole.
With two months to go to Election Day November 5, Clinton led Dole by 48.2 percent to 33.3 percent. Perot, running at the head of his own Reform Party, had 5.9 percent.
An ABC News/Washington Post poll released Thursday night gave Clinton an 11-point lead over Dole among likely voters, 51 to 40 percent, with Perot at seven percent.
